summary: Zhao Luo works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied under Sen Wang and held a post as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

Zhaohua Yang specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (faculty, attested 2018), and taught Kevin Buckelew.

Zhe Ji works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned a Ph.D. in sociology at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007 and was an Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
Zhen Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. Liu earned an MA from the University of Munich by 2005 and an MA from Lanzhou University by 2009.
Zhengyan Fan works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Fan has studied as a PhD researcher at Ghent University and held a post there as a PhD Researcher in 2026.

Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Buddhist College (1947) and under Yinshun (1952). He served as manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992) and taught Chien Y. Hsu.

Zhihua Yao specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel (~1997–2002) and held posts at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2005) and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2005).
Zhiqing Wang specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Wang studied at Lanzhou University from 2006 to 2009 and at East China Normal University in 2021.

Zhiru Ng works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Michigan (MA) under Luis Oscar Gómez and at the University of Arizona (PhD) under Robert M. Gimello.

Zhiru Shi (b. 1964) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello, later serving on the faculty at Pomona College.

Zhiyi Yang (b. 1979) specializes in Sinology. She studied at Peking University, University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Princeton University (PhD 2012 under Martin Kern), and became Professor (W3) at Goethe University Frankfurt in 2025.

Zhonghui Cui works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, serving there as a teaching consultant (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied under Su Bai (~1952–1956) and served as director of the Palace Museum (~1987–1991).

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960–1965), held a post there (~1965–1978), and was an Associate Professor at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002).
Zhuan Dao (1871–1943) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. He founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li works in Buddhist studies. Li studied at Komazawa University (attested 2015) and held a post as a JSPS DC research fellow (attested 2015).

Zolboo Sandagjav works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the National University of Mongolia, University of Delhi, University of Lausanne, and University of Bern, where he served as an assistant lecturer (2024–2025).

Zoltán Gombocz (1877–1935) was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Gimnázium and Eötvös Loránd University (1895–1900), and later taught Lajos Ligeti.

Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and Gyuto Monastery, serving as Abbot of Ganden Shartse (1937–1946) and later director and Rektor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Zongsan Mou (1909–1995) was a philosopher and Sinologist. He studied at Peking University under Shili Xiong, and held posts at institutions including Tunghai University, the University of Hong Kong, CUHK, and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies.
